headline: High: shared filesystem and broad tool/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee has session memory and handles documents/data; Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and shares state via local filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge where content from A can be ingested by B as trusted instructions. The interaction is documented enough to exceed low, but not enough for high because no direct shared channel is proven.
conditions: IF cognee outputs attacker-controlled text into a file or clipboard-accessible workspace
IF Windsurf ingests that content through workspace files or MCP without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Place cognee and Windsurf in separate directories
Require a manual review step before Windsurf follows file content
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while Windsurf reads workspace files and has broad network egress plus model-proxy/MCP calls. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive data can flow from A into B and then out through B's networked tools. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, but direct exfiltration is not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document set
IF Windsurf sends file contents to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory
Restrict Windsurf MCP servers to non-sensitive tasks
Review outbound requests before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on workspace reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; cognee supports multiple instances and session memory, so concurrent use over shared files can race or overwrite state. Because Windsurf's shared state is via local filesystem and cognee is not isolated at the OS level in the profile, the default overlap is dangerous and can corrupt work or git history.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF Windsurf auto-executes file edits while cognee updates related artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and Windsurf can act on workspace content with shell and git tools. That makes it plausible for Windsurf to treat cognee output as authoritative and then commit or execute changes without verification. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the blast radius is usually bounded to code or docs rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses cognee output as a source of truth
IF Windsurf executes or commits changes derived from that output without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before shell commands
Add a verification checklist for cognee-derived claims
Keep cognee outputs in a review-only folder
Limit Windsurf to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before actions

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Windsurf handles open files and may send content through a broad networked model proxy/MCP stack. If EU personal data or regulated records are placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create residency or retention mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in the workspace
IF Windsurf routes that data through external model or MCP services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use redacted copies for agent work
Document retention settings for both tools
Restrict external API use on sensitive projects
requires-engineering: map data residency and DPA obligations before deployment
